transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So with gardening, that's good news - you can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. Just avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for that info! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you don't have any left, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful! Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, that's quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. 

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let us know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. My final question is, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago. So it sounds like what I'm experiencing is normal. Thank you for answering all my questions. I've got no more questions for now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and remember to wear your sunglasses outside and follow all the advice we've discussed.
